chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In
a man who complained of his eyes, and kohl mixed with wine was described to him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is impure, like the dead body. If he is in need, let him use it for kohl.'

key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: The dead body (of an animal not slaughtered according to ritual)

ai.seo_question: Is kohl mixed with wine considered impure and permissible for use?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that kohl mixed with wine is ritually impure (khabith) and comparable to the dead body (maytah), reflecting the broader Shia juristic consensus on the impurity of wine. However, he permits its external use for eye treatment in cases of necessity (darura), illustrating the principle of 'removal of hardship' where the impurity does not render the treatment invalid when no alternative is available.
